note: 22 cards from online trends, each with one home pillar.

cards.card: Before bed, write tomorrow's to-do list for 5 minutes
cards.why: Writing it down lets your mind let go. Students who wrote tomorrow's to-do list before bed fell asleep faster.

cards.card: Go somewhere alone you'd usually save for company, like a gallery
cards.why: Going alone beats what you'd expect. People enjoyed a gallery on their own as much as those who went with a friend.

cards.card: Explore one spot in your new area on your own, like a park or market
cards.why: Exploring alone can be a real pleasure. People enjoyed a gallery on their own as much as those who went with a friend.

cards.card: Write five small things that lift you, then do one of them today
cards.why: Planning small good things lifts a low mood. Students who planned enjoyable things for two weeks felt much less low.

cards.card: Plan one small nice thing for today, and slow down to enjoy it
cards.why: Enjoying it on purpose makes it count. Students who planned something enjoyable and savoured it had more good feelings.

cards.card: Write your wish, the best result, what's in the way, and “If ___, I'll ___”
cards.why: Planning for the obstacle helps you start. Students who did this planned about twice as many hours for their goal.

cards.card: Sit for 10 minutes with nothing in your hands, and let your mind wander
cards.why: Your thoughts are better company than you'd guess. Students enjoyed time alone with their thoughts more than they expected.

cards.card: Wait without your phone today, in a queue or on the bus
cards.why: Time to just think is nicer than it sounds. Students left alone with their thoughts enjoyed it more than they predicted.

cards.card: Go for a 10-minute walk or wheel, just because
cards.why: A short walk lifts your mood. Young adults felt better after one, even when they expected it to be boring.

cards.card: Take the stairs fast, three times today
cards.why: Short bursts add up. Inactive young adults who climbed three flights fast, three times a day, got fitter in six weeks.

for: Meet new people (incl. starting from scratch)
cards.card: Give someone a real compliment today, like on their jacket or their idea
cards.why: Compliments land better than you fear. People giving them expected awkwardness, but the other person felt good.

cards.card: Leave a kind note for a flatmate, coworker or classmate
cards.why: Small kindness goes further than you think. People who got one felt far better than the giver expected.

cards.card: Write a short card to someone in your family, and give it or post it
cards.why: A short note means more than you'd guess. People who got a card from a student were far happier than the writer expected.

cards.card: Ask a friend one deeper question, like “What's been on your mind lately?”
cards.why: Deep talk goes better than you'd expect. People who talked about deeper things found it less awkward and more connecting.

cards.card: Colour in for 10 minutes: a free printable, or patterns you draw yourself
cards.why: Colouring can settle your mind. Women who coloured 10 minutes a day for a week felt less anxious and low.

cards.card: Do 15 minutes of strength moves, like squats, push-ups and lunges
cards.why: Strength work helps your head too. A review of 33 trials found it clearly eased low mood.

cards.card: Close your eyes and relive a happy memory for 10 minutes, like a trip
cards.why: Good memories can lift today. Students who pictured happy memories twice a day for a week felt happy more often.

cards.card: Before something stressful, rest a hand on your heart for 20 seconds
cards.why: Your own touch can calm your body. Young adults who did this before a stressful task had lower stress hormones.

cards.card: Do a chore slowly, like washing up, noticing the warmth and smells
cards.why: Slowing down turns a chore into a break. Students who washed dishes this way felt 27% less nervous afterwards.

cards.card: Put on a song that lifts you, and really try to feel it
cards.why: Trying helps the music work. People who tried to feel happier while listening to upbeat music did; just listening didn't.

cards.card: After reading for work or study, close it and write what you remember
cards.why: Testing yourself beats re-reading. A week after reading a passage, students who tested themselves remembered 61%, not 40%.
